hero.title: Code
hero.lede: The numerical codes behind the modelling work: two that I write and maintain, and the community codes I contribute to.

intro: Most of my results come out of simulations, so the code is part of the research rather than a tool beside it. Both of my own codes are written in Julia, documented in full, and benchmarked against published reference cases before they are used for science.

projects.name: MILEVA
projects.expansion: Mantle Interaction and Lithospheric Evolution in Viscous Annuli
projects.tagline: A finite-volume mantle-convection code in Julia.

facts.label: Geometry
facts.value: 2-D spherical and cylindrical annulus · 3-D spherical chunk and Yin-Yang sphere

projects.summary: MILEVA simulates thermal and compositional convection in Earth-like and planetary mantles. It solves the coupled Stokes, energy and composition equations on a staggered finite-volume grid, with velocities on cell faces and pressure at cell centres, while temperature and composition ride on Lagrangian markers.
projects.architecture: A flat-include research code. include/mileva.jl pulls in config/, utils/, markers/, physics/, solvers/ and parallel/; main_SphCon.jl holds the time loop.
projects.runNote: A run is a Julia script: edit the three configuration structs cfg, mat and temp, then call main_SphCon. VTK frames, checkpoints and diagnostics.csv land in cfg.outputDir.

media.caption: Three-dimensional plumes in the Yin-Yang spherical shell at Ra = 10^6.
Viscosity over 1 Gyr in the 2-D spherical annulus, with three continental rafts. Model R of van der Wiel et al. (2024).

sections.title: Physics
items: Thermochemical Stokes flow with the full deviatoric stress at variable viscosity, in Boussinesq or anelastic form.
Composite rheology: diffusion and dislocation creep, Arrhenius and Frank-Kamenetskii laws, yielding, viscoelastoplasticity, damage and grain-size evolution.
Thermal and compositional buoyancy: basalt, depletion, thermochemical piles and phase transitions.
Partial melting with depletion feedback, eruption, intrusion and heat-pipe cooling.
Radiogenic heating, fixed or cooling core boundaries, a free surface and isostasy.

sections.title: Numerics and solvers
items: Direct solvers including MUMPS in 2-D, geometric multigrid, and MPI domain decomposition.
Stokes solvers that hold up at viscosity contrasts to 10^18.
Conservative markers, with the energy budget logged on every run.

sections.title: Verification
items: The 2-D annulus is checked against Hernlund & Tackley (2008) and the annulus column of Fleury et al. (2024).
Conservation identities are checked every run.
The primordial-material case reproduces reference case M100dD of Gülcher, Ballmer & Tackley (2021).

projects.name: MILET
projects.tagline: A thermomechanical finite-element framework for lithosphere and mantle dynamics.
projects.summary: MILET couples Stokes flow to heat transport on an inf-sup stable Taylor–Hood discretisation, with material carried by markers. It is built for problems where composition, rheology and metamorphic phase change evolve together: lithospheric foundering, delamination, drips and subduction.
projects.architecture: Built on Gridap.jl. Runs are driven from main.jl; shipped cases include SolCx, Blankenbach 1a, subduction and a 3-D plume run on the multigrid solver.
projects.runNote: Each simulation is a TOML parameter file merged onto cases/_defaults.toml. Results are written to output/<case>/ and viewed in ParaView.

media.caption: Three-dimensional thermal convection in a box at Ra = 10^5.
Subduction in 2-D, reproducing Model 1 of Glerum et al. (2018).

sections.title: Physics
items: Incompressible Boussinesq and truncated anelastic liquid approximation (TALA) Stokes flow; markers carry composition, temperature, stress, plastic strain, grain size and porosity.
Visco-elasto-plastic composite creep with Drucker–Prager yield, strain softening and Arrhenius healing.
Rate-limited divariant metamorphic reactions with reaction-progress softening, and melting with melt weakening.
McKenzie-type two-phase flow: porous melt migration through a compacting matrix, reducing to single-phase Stokes at zero porosity.
Grain growth balanced against paleowattmeter reduction, coupled back into the creep mechanisms.
Shear, adiabatic and radiogenic heating; sticky-air and ALE free surfaces.

sections.title: Numerics and solvers
items: Direct (MUMPS) and iterative solvers, including a geometric-multigrid FGMRES solver for 3-D Stokes.
Picard and Newton nonlinear loops with CFL-limited time stepping.
Adaptive mesh refinement, checkpoint/restart and VTK output for ParaView.

sections.title: Verification
items: SolCx Stokes benchmark (Duretz et al. 2011).
Blankenbach et al. (1989) case 1a.
Smoke and benchmark tests shipped under test/.

contributionsLede: Alongside my own codes I contribute modules, benchmarks and post-processing to established open-source codes in the field.

contributions.name: ASPECT
contributions.desc: Planetary interior contributions: non-Newtonian viscosity laws for stagnant-lid regimes, thermal boundary-condition modules for Venus and Mars, and benchmarks for plume–lithosphere interaction under single-lid conditions.

contributions.name: LaMEM
contributions.desc: Ice-shell rheology for icy-moon applications, cryogenic extensions of the viscoelastoplastic constitutive laws, parallel scaling benchmarks, and graben and thrust-fault test cases.

contributions.name: iSALE
contributions.desc: Post-processing for impact melt volume, shock-pressure mapping and tectonic response; equation-of-state tables for planetary silicates and ices; visualisation tools extending pySALEPlot to multi-layer icy targets.
